tasks.title: NEW module ngv2/poc_writer.py — automated PoC synthesis core (P4.2)
acceptance_criteria: NEW file ngv2/poc_writer.py is created (it does NOT exist at HEAD) and contains EXACTLY the validated whole-file content given in the brief (including the module docstring, dataclasses Grounding, CWETemplate, PoCArtifact, and all per-CWE renderers).

Exposes synthesize(finding, target, *, client=None, resolver=None) -> PoCArtifact, write_poc(...), draft_poc(...), ground_finding(...), default_resolver(...), get_template(...), PER_CWE_TEMPLATES, Grounding, CWETemplate, PoCArtifact.

Pre-grounding via ground_finding resolves the real vulnerable symbol/module/entrypoint from the finding's evidence via default_resolver (or an injected resolver seam), defaulting to a stdlib-AST extractor over the cited file.

Carries templates for CWE-502 (__reduce__), CWE-95 (__import__('os').system), CWE-918 (metadata-IP + canary), CWE-78 (; <cmd> #), CWE-89 (stacked SQLi), CWE-798 (hardcoded secret), and CWE-327 (weak crypto) keyed by both canonical CWE id and pattern id.
write_poc and synthesize support dual Python + Node.js PoC generation reaching the actual vulnerable sink with a harmless marker ('VULNERABLE') and filesystem side-effect ('pwned_marker').

Supports optionally refining the skeleton via an injected LLM-client complete_text method, accepting the refined draft only if it contains the grounded module and the template marker, else falling back to the deterministic skeleton.
draft_poc supports threading feedback (failed detonation stderr + fs-diff) into the LLM prompt when feedback is supplied and a client is present, otherwise falling back to fresh synthesis.

spec.objective: Create the NEW module ngv2/poc_writer.py: a pure Python PoC synthesis core that, given a Finding, Target, and per-CWE template, synthesizes a runnable PoC (both Python and Node.js) that reaches the actual vulnerable sink.
functional_requirements: Implement default_resolver using stdlib AST to parse the cited source file and extract functions/constants relevant to the finding's CWE.
Implement ground_finding which resolves the vulnerable module and symbol using the resolver function.
Implement get_template to retrieve templates by CWE id or scanner pattern name.
Implement write_poc to render the skeleton for a specific language (python or node), refine it using the optional client if provided, validate, and return the PoC object.
Implement synthesize to produce both Python and Node.js PoCs inside a PoCArtifact.
Implement draft_poc to expose the P4.3 hook with repair feedback capability.
No network or third-party packages; standard library and ngv2.contracts only.
spec.interfaces: ngv2/poc_writer.py exposes: `synthesize(finding, target, *, client=None, resolver=None) -> PoCArtifact`, `write_poc(...)`, `draft_poc(...)`, `ground_finding(...)`, `default_resolver(...)`, `get_template(...)`, `PER_CWE_TEMPLATES`, `Grounding`, `CWETemplate`, `PoCArtifact`.
edge_cases: resolver returns dict instead of Grounding instance -> ground_finding tolerates and converts it.
language is other than python/py/python3 or node/js/javascript -> write_poc raises ValueError.
pre-grounding yields no module or symbols -> write_poc raises ValueError.
client complete_text raises an exception -> fallback to deterministic skeleton.
client refined draft lacks grounded module or template marker -> fallback to deterministic skeleton.
non_goals: Do NOT author or modify any tests; the committed oracle tests/test_poc_writer_wired.py is authoritative.
Do NOT make file or network I/O beyond reading the target source file in default_resolver.
Do NOT import ngv2.llm_client or any third-party packages.
Integration testing is OUT OF SCOPE: no integration or e2e tests are written since the detonate -> repair loop is P4.3.
spec.implementation_notes:
The module must match the complete code structure provided in the brief Deliverables. Keep all AST-based symbol ranking and CWE template configurations intact. Take care that credential-naming constraints (e.g. key, secret, password) do not trigger security gate failures.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.


# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/test_poc_writer_wired.py
```python
"""Oracle for P4.2 -- ngv2.poc_writer synthesis core.

Hermetic: no network (client is injected/None), no jail. Drives the REAL 5
synthetic targets (_e2e_run/targets/<pattern>/svc.py) and asserts:
  * the per-CWE template library covers all 5 live CWEs + ported CWE-502/918;
  * mandatory pre-grounding resolves the REAL vulnerable symbol from source
    (lookup_host / calc / find_user / API_KEY / reset_token) -- not a guess;
  * synthesize() emits a dual Python + Node.js PoC, each binding to the grounded
    symbol, carrying the marker + fs side-effect;
  * the synthesized Python PoC reproduces the load-bearing structure of the
    hand-written drive_one PoCs (the Phase-4 acceptance shape);
  * an injected client can refine but a bad refinement falls back to the
    verified skeleton.
RED until ngv2/poc_writer.py exists.
"""
import os

import pytest

from ngv2.contracts import Finding, PoC, Target
from ngv2.poc_writer import (
    PER_CWE_TEMPLATES,
    get_template,
    ground_finding,
    write_poc,
    synthesize,
    draft_poc,
    Grounding,
)

TARGETS_DIR = os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
    "_e2e_run", "targets",
)

# pattern -> (cwe, real symbol the PoC must bind to, severity, category)
LIVE = {
    "command_injection": ("CWE-78", "lookup_host", "critical"),
    "eval_usage": ("CWE-95", "calc", "high"),
    "sql_injection": ("CWE-89", "find_user", "high"),
    "hardcoded_secret": ("CWE-798", "API_KEY", "high"),
    "weak_crypto": ("CWE-327", "reset_token", "medium"),
}


def _finding(pattern, cwe, severity):
    svc = os.path.join(TARGETS_DIR, pattern, "svc.py")
    return Finding(
        id="F1", target=os.path.join(TARGETS_DIR, pattern), category=pattern,
        severity=severity, title=f"{cwe} in {pattern}",
        description=f"vuln {pattern}", evidence=[f"{svc}:1"],
    )


def _target(pattern):
    return Target(
        repo_url="https://example/x", repo_root=os.path.join(TARGETS_DIR, pattern),
        pinned_commit="deadbeef", language="python", loc=10,
    )


# --- template library coverage ---

def test_template_library_covers_ported_cwes():
    for cwe in ("CWE-502", "CWE-95", "CWE-918", "CWE-78", "CWE-89",
                "CWE-798", "CWE-327"):
        t = PER_CWE_TEMPLATES[cwe]
        assert t.cwe == cwe
        assert callable(t.render_py) and callable(t.render_js)
        assert t.marker == "VULNERABLE"


def test_template_resolves_by_pattern_alias():
    assert get_template("command_injection").cwe == "CWE-78"
    assert get_template("CWE-78").cwe == "CWE-78"


# --- mandatory pre-grounding resolves the REAL symbol ---

@pytest.mark.parametrize("pattern", sorted(LIVE))
def test_pre_grounding_resolves_real_symbol(pattern):
    cwe, real_symbol, sev = LIVE[pattern]
    g = ground_finding(_finding(pattern, cwe, sev), _target(pattern))
    assert isinstance(g, Grounding)
    assert g.module == "svc"
    assert real_symbol in g.symbols, (pattern, g.symbols)
    # sink-bearing symbol ranked first for the call-style CWEs
    if pattern in ("command_injection", "eval_usage"):
        assert g.symbols[0] == real_symbol


# --- dual output + binding to the real symbol ---

@pytest.mark.parametrize("pattern", sorted(LIVE))
def test_synthesize_dual_output_binds_real_symbol(pattern):
    cwe, real_symbol, sev = LIVE[pattern]
    art = synthesize(_finding(pattern, cwe, sev), _target(pattern))
    assert art.cwe == cwe
    assert art.marker == "VULNERABLE"
    assert art.fs_signature == "pwned_marker"
    assert isinstance(art.python, PoC) and art.python.language == "python"
    assert isinstance(art.node, PoC) and art.node.language == "node"
    art.python.validate()
    art.node.validate()
    # both bind to the grounded module + the real symbol
    for poc in (art.python, art.node):
        assert "svc" in poc.code
        assert real_symbol in poc.code
        assert "VULNERABLE" in poc.code
    # entrypoints are runnable by the live jail runner
    assert art.python.entrypoint == "python3 {poc}"
    assert art.node.entrypoint == "node {poc}"


# --- reproduces the load-bearing structure of the hand-written PoCs ---

def test_reproduces_handwritten_cmd_injection_shape():
    art = synthesize(_finding("command_injection", "CWE-78", "critical"),
                     _target("command_injection"))
    code = art.python.code
    assert "from svc import lookup_host" in code
    assert "lookup_host(" in code
    assert "; echo VULNERABLE" in code
    assert ": > pwned_marker" in code


def test_reproduces_handwritten_eval_shape():
    art = synthesize(_finding("eval_usage", "CWE-95", "high"),
                     _target("eval_usage"))
    code = art.python.code
    assert "from svc import calc" in code
    assert "__import__('os').system(" in code
    assert "VULNERABLE" in code


def test_reproduces_handwritten_secret_shape():
    art = synthesize(_finding("hardcoded_secret", "CWE-798", "high"),
                     _target("hardcoded_secret"))
    code = art.python.code
    assert "from svc import API_KEY" in code
    assert "pwned_marker" in code


# --- injected client: refine vs fall back to verified skeleton ---

def test_client_refinement_accepted_when_sound():
    cwe, sym, sev = LIVE["command_injection"]

    class GoodClient:
        def complete_text(self, prompt, *, system=None):
            # a sound refinement keeps svc + marker
            return ("import sys\nsys.path.insert(0, '/x')\n"
                    "from svc import lookup_host\n"
                    "lookup_host('localhost; echo VULNERABLE; : > pwned_marker')\n"
                    "# refined\n")

    poc = write_poc(_finding("command_injection", cwe, sev),
                    _target("command_injection"), client=GoodClient())
    assert "# refined" in poc.code


def test_bad_client_refinement_falls_back_to_skeleton():
    cwe, sym, sev = LIVE["command_injection"]

    class BadClient:
        def complete_text(self, prompt, *, system=None):
            return "print('nope')\n"  # drops svc + marker -> rejected

    poc = write_poc(_finding("command_injection", cwe, sev),
                    _target("command_injection"), client=BadClient())
    assert "from svc import lookup_host" in poc.code
    assert "VULNERABLE" in poc.code


def test_draft_poc_repair_threads_feedback():
    seen = {}

    class Client:
        def complete_text(self, prompt, *, system=None):
            seen["prompt"] = prompt
            # echo back the verified skeleton region so it passes the soundness gate
            return ("from svc import lookup_host\nlookup_host('x; echo VULNERABLE; "
                    ": > pwned_marker')\nimport svc  # repaired\n")

    art = draft_poc(_finding("command_injection", "CWE-78", "critical"),
                    _target("command_injection"), client=Client(),
                    feedback="stderr: ModuleNotFoundError; fs-diff: <none>")
    assert "repaired" in art.python.code
    assert "fs-diff" in seen["prompt"]


def test_pre_grounding_failure_raises():
    # a finding pointing at a nonexistent file -> no symbols -> explicit error
    f = Finding(id="F9", target="/nope", category="command_injection",
                severity="high", title="x", description="y",
                evidence=["/does/not/exist.py:1"])
    t = Target(repo_url="u", repo_root="/nope", pinned_commit="c",
               language="python")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        write_poc(f, t)

```
